A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PPISP work and contain the main paper and supplementary Sections A-D. Text extraction and visual inspection establish that the equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original novel-view synthesis benchmarks, component ablations, metadata experiments, runtime measurements, and appendix calibration and exposure analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical studies and adds Zip-NeRF results, expanded 3DGS baseline comparisons, and perceptual color-error maps.

M1.justification: The four ISP modules, controller architecture, two-stage optimization, regularizers, and metadata inputs remain unchanged. Applying PPISP to Zip-NeRF provides another evaluation configuration without documenting a changed PPISP procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same benchmark datasets, PPISP/PPISP-auto captures, and SMERF diagnostic example. Existing examples move between Figures 4 and 5. Zip-NeRF is an added reconstruction model, not new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 substantially expands comparator coverage. The 3DGS blocks previously compared only unmodified 3DGS with PPISP; v2 adds BilaRF, ADOP, and GLO across four datasets. New Zip-NeRF blocks compare unmodified Zip-NeRF, BilaRF, and PPISP.

E3.justification: v2 adds a Zip-NeRF evaluation configuration on three existing datasets and CIEDE2000 error-map evaluation. Color-aligned metric reporting narrows from PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS to PSNR alone. The stated 30k-plus-5k training budgets and appendix splits and preprocessing remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 4 and 5 add spatial CIEDE2000 error maps, allowing localized photometric discrepancies to be examined in existing examples. Component and capacity ablations, ADOP diagnostics, camera calibration, and exposure-identifiability analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The appendix correlation and exposure-error analyses retain the same statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds substantial baseline and Zip-NeRF results, including BilaRF outperforming PPISP on the BilaRF dataset with Zip-NeRF: 22.94 versus 22.85 PSNR. Existing 3DGS+PPISP PSNR on BilaRF changes from 24.86 to 25.39 without an explanation of the revision. SSIM-CC and LPIPS-CC entries are removed; retained 3DGUT results and Tables 2-9 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, regularizers, exposure-ambiguity reasoning, and appendix homography construction and DLT-equivalence derivation are unchanged. Equation reflow and spelling corrections do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same core contributions and claims: physically grounded photometric correction, a controller enabling evaluation without target images, strong benchmark performance, intuitive control, and metadata integration. The expanded experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: The explanations of disentanglement, capacity versus generalization, and camera calibration remain substantively unchanged. Both versions retain limitations concerning local tone mapping, lens flares, and manual camera overrides. Section 5.1's revised performance summary reflects the expanded results rather than a new mechanism explanation.

D1.justification: The new Table 1 caption explicitly states that controller-free novel views use zero per-frame corrections. Section 5 clarifies MCMC's application to 3DGS and 3DGUT. These are documentation refinements; controller specifications, optimizer schedules, hardware information, and access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work adds Block-NeRF, Neural Lens Modeling, and HDR-GS, expanding discussion of exposure conditioning and physical imaging models. Additional technical citations cover Zip-NeRF, MCMC, CIEDE2000, and Debevec-Malik. ADOP remains the closest predecessor and the central novelty positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 corrects grammar and terminology, condenses selected related-work and experiment passages, revises captions, and updates acknowledgments. The main section sequence and supplementary organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 is rebuilt from a full-width six-metric table into a compact four-metric display grouped by reconstruction model. Figures 4 and 5 are substantially redesigned around ground-truth panels and error maps, with existing examples redistributed between them. These changes materially restructure the central empirical presentation.

improvement.justification: The expanded 3DGS comparisons and Zip-NeRF tests in Table 1 better substantiate comparative performance and applicability beyond Gaussian reconstruction, including a disclosed case where BilaRF wins. Error maps make residual discrepancies easier to assess. The overall gain is incremental, with reduced aligned-metric reporting and unexplained revisions to existing 3DGS scores limiting transparency.
